title: Prefetch Reliability: Telemetry Fusion & Operator Actionbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary

This actionbook defines the telemetry fusion, dashboards, alerting, and operator runbook for prefetch/prefix-KV cache reliability across the Redwood inference platform. It focuses on synthesizing signals from cache-layer telemetry, scheduler and allocator metrics, request path traces, and tenant cost signals into clear operator actions that protect SLOs while minimizing unnecessary throttling or evictions.

Intent and scope

- Intent: Reduce mean time to remediate (MTTR) for prefetch-related degradations and reduce unnecessary tenant impact from overaggressive prefetch throttles.
- Scope: Global runtime prefix/KV caches, edge prefetch hints, platform prefetch orchestration service (prefetchd), and operator-facing dashboards. Does NOT cover model-level KV correctness or client-side cache instrumentation.

Owners and contacts

- Primary owner: eng-platform (prefetch & cache subteam)
- Runbook author: Aisha Kapoor
- Pager: eng-platform oncall rotation (see /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/platform-oncall-quick-reference-shell-helpers-and-scripts-2026)
- Escalation path: oncall -> pref-caching-owners -> runtime-sre -> eng-sre director

SLOs and guardrails

| SLO / Metric | Target | Action tier |
|---|---:|---|
| Median prefix cache hit rate (global aggregate, 1h) | >= 72% | Informational |
| 95th %-tile token latency for foreground requests | <= 220 ms | Tier 1 (alert) |
| Global prefetchd error rate (5m) | <= 0.5% | Tier 1 (alert) |
| Tenant-prefetch-throttle-count (per-tenant, 5m) | <= 5/min | Tier 2 (operator review) |
| Prewarm/cold-start spike frequency (region, 1d) | <= 3 | Tier 2 |

Observability signals to fuse

- Cache-layer: hit/miss counts, eviction rates, per-prefix miss latency, KV read/write errors, prefix memory pressure.
- Prefetch orchestration (prefetchd): enqueue latency, worker concurrency, backpressure signals, per-tenant prefetch success/failure.
- Serving runtime: long-tail token latency, queueing time, batch formation delays.
- Scheduler/allocator: GPU utilization, contention metrics, preemption events.
- Telemetry cross-signal: correlated increase in token latency + rising miss rate + surge in tenant prefetch attempts = high-confidence prefetch degradation.

Dashboard and panel guidance

Recommended dashboard (single page for incidents):
1) Global summary row: global hit rate, global 95p token latency, prefetchd error rate, global memory fill%.
2) Time-series panels: per-region hit/miss rate, eviction rate, worker queue depth for prefetchd, allocator pressure.
3) Heatmap: per-tenant sudden-miss-rate-deltas (last 5m vs last 1h) with sortable tenant column.
4) Trace sampler: linked request traces for top 10 slow requests with KV miss annotations.
5) Cost overlay: token cost delta (last 1h) to catch runaway tenants.

Panel configuration notes:
- Use 1m rollup for high sensitivity panels (alerting); 5m for operator-facing trend panels.
- Annotate automated remediation windows and recent configuration changes (auto-inject changelog via CI tags).

Alert definitions and routing

- Alert: Prefetchd_Error_Rate_High
  - Trigger: prefetchd error rate > 1.0% for 5m
  - Severity: P1
  - Pager: eng-platform oncall, runtime-sre (channel: #prefetchd-pager)
  - Runbook ref: detection -> step 1 in this document

- Alert: Cache_HitRate_Degraded
  - Trigger: region hit rate drop >= 20% vs 1h baseline AND 95p token latency > SLO for 5m
  - Severity: P1/P2 depending on tenant impact
  - Pager: eng-platform oncall

- Alert: Tenant_Prefetch_Storm
  - Trigger: single-tenant prefetch throttle count > 50 in 5m or prefetchd enqueue growth > 5x
  - Severity: P2
  - Pager: infra-owner + customer-success (if enterprise tenant)

Operator runbook (detection -> remediation)

Detection and triage (steps to follow when a P1 fires)
1) Confirm alert: open dashboard, validate signal specificity. Correlate with deploy changelog (last 30m).
2) Run quick query (Grafana/PromQL or BigQuery): per-region hit/miss, kernel-level GPU pressure, and prefetchd queue depth. Copy links to incident.
3) Attach 3 representative traces (fastest, median, slowest) for the last 5 minutes to the incident page.

Diagnosis checklist
- Is the degradation localized to one region or global?
- Are there concurrent deploys or config changes? (CI annotation panel)
- Is the allocator reporting preemption or warmset churn?
- Are eviction rates increasing prior to latency? (sign of mem pressure)
- Is a single tenant causing disproportionate miss activity?

Automated quick fixes (safe to run without approval)
- If prefetchd worker queue depth is high and error rate is low: increase prefetchd worker concurrency by +20% (via feature toggle) for up to 15 minutes.
  - Command example: curl -X POST https://ops-api/internal/prefetchd/scale -d '{"delta_pct":20}' 
- If eviction rate > 2x baseline and memory pressure high: temporarily increase cache soft-limit (global) by 5% and mark as auto-scaled.
  - CLI example: /ops/cachectl set-soft-limit --region eu-west-1 --pct +5

Manual operator remediations (when automated fixes do not resolve)
1) Region isolation: divert <10% of incoming traffic from affected region to healthy region using the traffic-shepherd service. Follow the safe-stepdown checklist in the traffic-shepherd UI (do not exceed cross-region burst credits).
2) Tenant throttling: identify the noisy tenant from heatmap and apply a soft throttle (graceful degrade) to prefetch attempts for that tenant only. Notify customer-success for enterprise tenants.
   - Example: /ops/tenantctl throttle set --tenant t-1234 --prefetch-rate 1/s --duration 10m --reason "auto-throttle-investigation"
3) Controlled cache eviction: for catastrophic memory pressure, trigger a tiered eviction that evicts coldest prefixes first. Use eviction-safe mode to avoid evicting pinned prefixes.

Rollback and post-fix verification
- Verification checklist after any remediation: global 95p token latency back under SLO for 10m AND hit rate returning to baseline within 20% of pre-incident level.
- If verification fails, escalate per escalation path. Document action IDs for automated commands.

Planned runbook drills and testing

- Monthly synthetic lab: inject controlled miss storm for a shadow tenant and rehearse the automated scaling and tenant-throttle play. Measure MTTR and false-positive throttle rate.
- Quarterly cross-team game day: include customer-success and go-to-market for enterprise impact simulation.

Rollout guidance for prefetch tuning changes

1) Canary: deploy config change to 1 region (non-peak) for 2 hours with synthetic traffic ramp.
2) Canary metrics to watch: prefetchd enqueue latency, region hit rate, eviction spike, per-tenant throttle count.
3) Gradual rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with 30m observation windows.
4) Post-rollout retrospective: capture tuning delta, regressions, and update this document.

Post-incident retro template (use after any P1 caused by prefetch)

- Incident summary (one paragraph)
- Timeline: detection -> diagnosis -> remediation -> verification
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence
- What went well (automation, runbook clarity)
- What failed (dashboards, signal gaps, noisy alerts)
- Action items (owner, due date, verification step)

Appendix: CLI snippets and helpful queries

- Query: per-tenant miss delta (PromQL):
  increase(prefix_miss_count{region="eu-west-1"}[5m]) / increase(prefix_miss_count{region="eu-west-1"}[1h])

- Eviction check (SQL):
  SELECT region, prefix, SUM(evictions) as evic_sum FROM cache_eviction_events WHERE ts > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR) GROUP BY region, prefix ORDER BY evic_sum DESC LIMIT 50;

- Safe autoscale API: POST /ops/prefetchd/autoscale {"region":"us-west-2", "scale_pct": 20, "duration_min": 15}

Glossary

- prefetchd: platform orchestration service that schedules background prefetches of KV prefixes.
- prefix/KV cache: in-memory store keyed by model prefix used to accelerate autoregressive decoding.
- hot prefix: prefix with > 1000 hits/min in a region.
